properties.name: DEFECT (measured 2026-10-01): a one-shot `--call` run in a folder whose .reflow2.toml names a hosted design ignores the pointer AND --only-if-present, and CREATES a fresh local store with a newly minted id — the stray-store hazard the pointer exists to stop
properties.statement:
OBSERVED while moving nymath's design to flo2.io (dad8f529a065ac9b), from the dev_reflow2 hub session.
- Setup: nymath had just been given a .reflow2.toml naming https://api.flo2.io/g/dad8f529a065ac9b/mcp, and its old store had been moved aside.
- Command: `reflow2-mcp --graph-path .reflow2/graph --shared --only-if-present --call design_identity`, the user-scope MCP entry's own arguments plus --call, run in that folder.
- Result: graph_id 4e342661a79ba9af, label "nymath", origin "minted". A NEW empty store at nymath/.reflow2 that names itself after the folder. It was removed at once after confirming 0 nodes.

WHY, read from origin/main crates/reflow2-mcp/src/main.rs (~1645–1690):
- The pointer check ("A FOLDER THAT NAMES ITS DESIGN FOLLOWS THE NAME") and the latent --only-if-present check both run only AFTER every CLI-only mode has returned.
- So --call (and the other one-shot modes) never see either rule, and opening the graph creates it.
- The client path a harness uses (stdio, no --http, no --serve-shared) does follow the pointer, so a real session in the folder attaches correctly.

WHY IT MATTERS:
- A script, hook or person running a one-shot read in a moved design's folder silently gets a second, empty design with a fresh id beside the pointer.
- That is the frozen-store class of fact:an-agent-opened-in-a-moved-designs-folder-is-served-the-frozen-store-2026-09-27, by another door. The empty result reads as "nothing here" rather than as an error.

NOT ROOT-CAUSED beyond the ordering. Whether a one-shot mode should follow the pointer (forward the call), refuse with the pointer's address, or open the store only when it already exists is open.
